authorityBoundary: Computing research only; no expiry service, prior registry, model router or owner policy is authorized.
decision: Do not run F13 in Wave 3. Retain H-PRIOR-BIAS as an emerging cross-experiment finding; reopen revalidation/expiry only when a natural new task family supplies an independently fixed prior and post-change oracle.
question: Can explicit expiry/revalidation prevent retained adaptive priors from becoming harmful decision-boundary bias after model/task change?
reason: No materially distinct, prospectively scorable task family was found in which a previously earned semantic prior, a natural model/task change, and an independent downstream oracle coexist without reusing architecture/equipment promotion or capital-taxonomy outcomes. A model-change expiry rule built now would be tuned to the known F5/F6/F9 failure pattern. Mechanical stale-reference/currentness checks are not a substitute for semantic prior-bias evidence.
reopenConditions: A retained semantic prior was earned before a later model/provider/task-family change
The new task family has an owner-native or otherwise independent outcome oracle
Prior-on, prior-off and a predeclared revalidation/expiry treatment can be frozen before target outcomes are inspected
The experiment does not reuse F5/F6/F9 decision labels as its answer key
